slides.title: Macchiato doesn't mean "with milk"
slides.subtitle: The word describes what the espresso looks like.

slides.title: It means stained
slides.body: In Italian, macchiato means stained or marked. It comes from the verb macchiare, to stain, which traces back to a Latin word for spotted.

slides.title: So what gets stained?
slides.body: The espresso. A small spot of milk leaves a mark on top, so the drink stays mostly coffee. The milk is the stain, not the main event.

slides.label: At the bar
slides.body: Ask for a macchiato and you'll usually get espresso with a spot of milk. Say latte macchiato for the milky glass.

slides.title: Macchiato means marked, not milky
slides.body: Caffè macchiato: coffee marked with milk. Latte macchiato: milk marked with coffee.
slides.cta: Save it for your next order
